Use that origin for every NvStreamer API call in this task. Read `vss configure show` and set `VST_API_BASE` from `.services.vst.url` plus `/api/v1` for VIOS calls. These are separate services. Do not use sandbox localhost, infer an NvStreamer port from the VSS ingress, or guess a host/port. **Start fresh (idempotency on a reused box):** before uploading, delete any leftover `warehouse_safety_0001` from a prior run so the upload returns a clean HTTP 2xx instead of `400 InvalidParameterError "Sensor exists already"` — `curl -s -X DELETE ${VSS_STREAMER_URL%/}/api/v1/storage/file/warehouse_safety_0001` (the full-removal form with NO time range deletes the on-disk file too, so it will not re-appear on the next discovery/scan; also delete any deduplicated `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>` you see in `/api/v1/sensor/list`). A 404 / `"Failed find the stream object of the file"` when it is already absent is expected — ignore it. Then upload the sample warehouse safety video (warehouse_safety_0001) to NvStreamer via `POST /api/v1/storage/file` (single-chunk multipart, with the `nvstreamer-file-name` header), confirm the sensor via `GET /api/v1/sensor/list`, then look up the RTSP URL NvStreamer auto-generated for the file from the all-streams endpoint `GET /api/v1/sensor/streams` (the flattened `{<sensorId>: [stream, ...]}` array — NOT the per-sensor `/sensor/<id>/streams`, whose `url` can be empty). Finally, **verify the documented filename-validation rule by issuing a second POST upload with `nvstreamer-file-name: bad name.mp4`** (note the space) — the server must reject it with HTTP 400 and the body `{"error_code": "InvalidParameterError", "error_message": "Whitespaces not allowed in file name"}`, and the previously uploaded `warehouse_safety_0001` sensor must remain intact afterward.

**Environment & prerequisites:** Reuse the VIOS services deployed by the setup task. If a required service is unavailable, report the dependency failure without redeploying. **Readiness gate (run before any check):** a `/sensor/version` response is served by each service's control-plane process and goes healthy BEFORE that service finishes its first-boot `*_INSTALL_ADDITIONAL_PACKAGES` libav apt-install and full `launch_vst` startup, so probing upload / record / snapshot / timeline endpoints too early yields spurious `Failed to get media information` or empty-result failures. Before running any check, confirm the media backends are actually serving: for NvStreamer, the NvStreamer image contains its architecture-appropriate libavformat library (or a tiny known-good upload returns 2xx); for VIOS, `curl -sf ${VST_API_BASE}/live/version` AND `curl -sf ${VST_API_BASE}/record/version` each return HTTP 200 with a JSON body (both are streamprocessing-served, unlike `/sensor/version`; treat any non-empty version value as valid - do not assert a specific version). Allow up to ~120s on first boot before treating a failure as real. Exercise the NvStreamer API surface in `references/nvstreamer-api-reference.md` against the stack prepared by the setup task. **Reuse the SDRC-routed VIOS deployment from setup** (`VST_USE_SDRC=true`) — step-2's NvStreamer-to-VIOS RTSP handoff + recording rely on it. Host deployment configuration, image pulls and package installation were completed by setup; the operational sandbox needs no NGC credentials or Docker access. Confirm NvStreamer media readiness by performing the requested known-good upload; if it reports transient media initialization, allow up to 120 seconds before reporting failure. Use the prepared `/tmp/vss-sample-data/dev-profile-sample-data/warehouse_safety_0001.mp4` source; NemoClaw uses the sandbox copy staged by setup.
checks: The POST to http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/storage/file with the `nvstreamer-file-name: warehouse_safety_0001.mp4` header and a single multipart `file` part (i.e. `-F 'file=@/tmp/vss-sample-data/dev-profile-sample-data/warehouse_safety_0001.mp4;type=video/mp4'`, with NO `nvstreamer-chunk-*` / `nvstreamer-identifier` headers) returns HTTP 2xx with a JSON body containing non-empty `id` and `streamId` fields.

**POST-upload identifier semantics:** use the SAME successful NvStreamer single-part multipart POST response identified in the preceding check: `/api/v1/storage/file` at the origin from `nvstreamer_endpoint.json`, with `nvstreamer-file-name: warehouse_safety_0001.mp4` and no chunk headers. Its `id` and `streamId` are filename-based (NOT a UUID) — they equal `warehouse_safety_0001`, or the deduplicated form `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>` when a file of that name already exists (NvStreamer appends `_<N>` on a name collision, e.g. from a retried upload or a pre-existing file; the suffixed form still satisfies this check — the point is filename-based naming, not a UUID). The `sensorId` field is allowed to be returned as an empty string — read `id` / `streamId` instead, as documented in `references/nvstreamer-api-reference.md § 3 Method 3`. Correlate these identifiers with that response's `filePath` and `filename`. UUIDs from a VIOS upload/registration response, a different service origin, or a PUT/chunked upload are not evidence about this NvStreamer POST and must not determine this check's verdict.

The response's `filePath` ends with `${VST_CONTAINER_ROOT}/streamer_videos/warehouse_safety_0001.mp4` (or the deduplicated `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>.mp4` on a name collision), and `filename` equals the matching stem (`warehouse_safety_0001` or `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>`).

After a short delay, `curl -sf http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/list` returns a JSON array that CONTAINS an entry whose `sensorId` and `name` equal the id the upload returned in check 1 — `warehouse_safety_0001`, or the deduplicated `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>` on a name collision — and whose `type` is `sensor_nvstream`. Select that entry by the upload's returned id; the array MAY also contain other sensors (e.g. stale leftover sensors from earlier streams), so do NOT assert it is the only element — the check passes as long as the just-uploaded sensor is present.

Read the stream from the all-streams endpoint `curl -sf http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/streams` (an array of `{<sensorId>: [stream, ...]}`; flatten with `jq 'add'` and select the entry for the sensor id returned by the upload in check 1 — `warehouse_safety_0001` or the deduplicated `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>`) rather than the per-sensor `/sensor/<id>/streams` path. Its first element has a `url` field starting with `rtsp://` and containing the path `/nvstream/`. The host portion of the URL is non-empty (not the broken `rtsp://:31554/...` form). The stream's `type` is `Rtsp` and `storageLocation` is `Local`. The returned stream entry does NOT contain a `vodUrl` field — NvStreamer never emits one (documented in `references/nvstreamer-api-reference.md § 2`).

Posting the same file again with `nvstreamer-file-name: bad name.mp4` (containing a space) returns HTTP 400 `{"error_code": "InvalidParameterError", "error_message": "Whitespaces not allowed in file name"}` — confirms the filename-whitespace rule documented in `references/nvstreamer-api-reference.md § 3 Filename rule`. The previously uploaded `warehouse_safety_0001` sensor must still be intact after this rejected call.

If VIOS is NOT part of the deployment (NvStreamer-only profile or stream-processor not running), skip the registration step and report that the handoff is not applicable — do NOT attempt `/sensor/add`.

Preserve the complete RTSP URL returned for that NvStreamer sensor, including its host, selected RTSP port, and full /nvstream/... path. The HTTP ingress origin is only for control-plane API calls. VIOS consumes sensorUrl from its own container, so do not replace the RTSP host or port with the sandbox HTTP origin, use the HTTP port 31000 or 7777, or shorten the path.

An upload API or VIOS upload does not satisfy the filesystem-copy precondition, and a 404 from a wrong endpoint does not satisfy the list check.

`curl -s -X POST http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/scan -w '%{http_code}'` returns HTTP 200 with a body of `null` — the scan is async and does not include the new sensor list in its response.

After a 2–5 second wait, `/sensor/list` includes a new entry whose `name` matches the copied file's basename `<copied>` (or the uniqueified form `<copied>_<N>` if a name collision occurred) and whose `location` ends with `${VST_CONTAINER_ROOT}/streamer_videos/<copied>.mp4`. The entry's `type` is `sensor_nvstream` and `state` is `online`.

The all-streams endpoint `curl -sf http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/streams` (flatten the `{<sensorId>: [stream, ...]}` array and select the newly-added sensor's entry, rather than the per-sensor `/sensor/<id>/streams` path) returns a usable RTSP URL of the form `rtsp://<host>:<lb-port>/nvstream${VST_CONTAINER_ROOT}/streamer_videos/<copied>.mp4` for the copied file (note: NvStreamer joins the `/nvstream` prefix directly to the absolute container path, so with `VST_CONTAINER_ROOT=/home/vst/vst_release` the rendered path is the single-slash `/nvstream/home/vst/vst_release/streamer_videos/<copied>.mp4`, NOT a double slash). The `<lb-port>` lies within NvStreamer's configured RTSP server pool (default `31554`–`31561`). For NemoClaw, <copied> must come from this trial's passed host-fixture receipt and the sandbox nvstreamer_scan.json manifest, matching the pre-scan absence and post-scan sensor checks above. Select that new sensorId in the all-streams response. Ignore any different filename from setup or an earlier task's Docker copy; it is not this trial's declared scan fixture. For other harnesses, use the unique basename from this task's own Docker copy. Include the matching sensorId and returned RTSP URI in the evidence.

`curl -sf -o /tmp/nvs-frame.jpg -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/live/stream/<new-sensorId>/picture?frameId=0` returns `200 image/jpeg`, the saved file is larger than 500 bytes, and `file /tmp/nvs-frame.jpg` reports `JPEG image data` (confirms the file is playable, not just present as a directory entry). Resolve <new-sensorId> from the post-scan sensor/list entry whose name equals <copied> from this trial's host-fixture receipt or Docker copy. Use that exact sensorId in the picture request and include it in the matched evidence. A JPEG from warehouse_safety_0001 or another pre-existing sensor does not pass the newly scanned file's playability check.

Calling `/live/stream/<new-sensorId>/picture` with NEITHER `frameId` NOR `startTime` returns HTTP 500 — proving `/picture` needs EITHER a `frameId` OR a `startTime` (they are alternatives, not `frameId`-only). The current build's body is `{"error_code": "VMSInternalError", "error_message": "Wrong time format or frameId provided"}`; accept that exact body OR any HTTP 500 whose message indicates a `frameId`/`startTime` is required. See `references/nvstreamer-api-reference.md § 5`.
